dedupe_keys.name: paysim mobile money payment simulator for fraud detection multi agent

description: PaySim is a multi-agent based simulator of a mobile money service, in which phone users transfer money as an electronic wallet, built to generate synthetic transaction logs for fraud detection research. The GitHub README read on 2026-09-26 says the first phase modelled the real service's schema with predicted scenarios, and the second used aggregated real transaction logs so that generated data resemble the original; a 2019 contribution with the company Flaminem added money laundering cases. It is led by Edgar Lopez-Rojas, grew from a research project funded by the Swedish Knowledge Foundation, and is released under the GPL-3.0 licence, free, as Java code (version 2.0 in the Maven file) with parameter files; a sample dataset, PaySim1, is on Kaggle. Coverage is a single anonymised mobile money service. Caveats: the Kaggle sample could not be opened from this session, there are no tagged releases, and outputs are synthetic. For simulation it generates payment flows to test fraud detection and disruption of digital payment infrastructure. Related catalogue records include the Cash Usage Database and the IMF PortWatch data.
